title: decision-models-as-guardrails leaderboard results
description: What site/leaderboard/index.html renders. One entry per (implementation, view). The page also accepts the evaluator's native document (benchmark/goldrails_bench/leaderboard.py, schema goldrails-leaderboard/0.1) and converts it with leaderboard.js fromEvaluator, so a published run needs no hand conversion. Scoring follows the completion plan: task score = 100 x 0.5 x (violation recall + benign pass rate), suites averaged equally, overall ranked only when all six suites are evaluated.

schema_version.description: The page's display format. The evaluator's own output (benchmark/goldrails_bench/leaderboard.py, schema goldrails-leaderboard/0.1) is also accepted and converted in leaderboard.js (fromEvaluator).

placeholder.description: true for invented demonstration values. The page shows a banner and suffixes every label while this is true. A real export sets false.

split.description: test for published results. tune is allowed only for pipeline checks and the page labels it.

evaluation_contract.description: Path or version of the frozen evaluation contract.

public_note.description: How the public dataset version relates to the internal release these results use.

public_release.description: The public dataset version label, for example v0.0.1.

pricing_region.description: The one region whose rate prices every self-hosted GPU pass.

self_hosted_cost.description: How to read self-hosted costs, e.g. 'normalized estimate'.

run_locations.description: Where each self-hosted GPU pass actually ran, from cloud audit logs; kept apart from the pricing assumption.

suites.description: Optional display overrides. The page always shows the fixed tab set; this can only relabel or annotate it.

blockers.description: Publication blockers carried from the evaluator; the page lists them in the banner.

source.description: Where a converted document came from (evaluator schema, mode, validity).

corrections.description: Post-run corrections to scoring or reporting, newest first. The original results stay published beside them.

data_quality.description: Per suite: what the test rows are made of and what they can support.

review.description: Who reviewed these labels after their origin, e.g. 'project owner'. label_basis keeps the origin.

bias_parts.description: The bias assessment in three named parts, each answering one question. Values come from bias-parts.json (copied from bias.json) and row counts from bias-audit.json. Outside every score; no number combines the parts.

balanced_accuracy.description: Moderation quality guard on the B1 rows. Not a fairness measure.

b2.description: Decision consistency (flips) and correctness (both texts right) side by side.

disclosures.description: Known limits that do not block publication, e.g. a local baseline whose cost is not measured.

run.description: Which benchmark run this file shows, written for any run after the first (benchmark/runs/site_results.py). Its publication status from the evaluator, the previous run's status and results file (relative to the page, for index.html?results=), and what changed between the runs, copied from both final leaderboards.

provisional.description: Suites whose reference labels are provisional, and why.

sensitivity_views.description: Post-hoc sensitivity views committed after the data-quality review; shown beside, never in place of, primary scores.

label_review.description: A recorded human review of the current release's labels. Original label origins stay in each row and in data_quality.

scope.description: What is compared, what supplies the reference answers, the claim the results support, and what is not tested.

comparisons.description: Paired differences (a minus b on the same test rows) copied from the evaluator; verdicts come from these, not from overlap of separate intervals.

accepted_blockers.description: Evaluator publication blockers the project owner accepted in a committed, confirmed approval, with the basis.

method.description: For example: paired group bootstrap over conversation/source/attack groups, 2000 resamples.

sweep.description: Set only for a genuine configuration sweep that changes measured work (single pass vs cascade, batching). Never for a threshold change.

scope.description: Views this implementation appears in. Omitted means every view, with a labelled not-evaluated row where it has no entry.

track.description: Bias only: guardrail_fairness covers B1/B2, decision_bias covers B3.

status.description: Only evaluated entries are plotted. not_applicable is used, for example, for Bedrock on B3 decision tasks; it is never scored as zero.

missing_suites.description: Overall only: suites that stop the overall score from being ranked.

conditional_score.description: Score over decided rows only, shown beside the primary score.

components.description: Overall only: the six suite scores the aggregate averages.

value.description: Numeric cut, or a label such as 'service operating point' for a binary service.

recovered_after_failure.description: Rows that failed in the original run and succeeded when re-attempted under the same frozen configuration. Both runs are charged in cost.

cost.description: Null when not measured. A value of zero is never a default: the page refuses to plot 0 on a cost axis and flags it.

usd_per_1000.description: Zero is allowed only with zero_tariff: true (a documented zero list price, for example a free policy). The page never plots zero on the log axis.

estimate.description: Self-hosted only: what the cost is normalized to and where the pass ran.

basis.description: How latency was measured, e.g. serial (one request at a time) or under the test pass's declared concurrency.

loaded_p95_s.description: p95 under the test pass's declared concurrency, kept for reference; not comparable across systems.

source_metric.description: B3: the source-defined metric name, e.g. discrim-eval logit gap or BBQ bias score.

sensitivity.description: A declared sensitivity analysis shown beside the primary score, never replacing it.

suites.description: Overall entries only: each suite's score for this implementation, including composed suites such as word filters (custom words and profanity, equal weight).

bias_interval.description: A bootstrap interval copied from bias.json (via bias-parts.json); draw counts stay in bias.json.
